subject.title: [BUG] OpenAI Codex errors leak into user chat

question: Should #44910 be resolved as a parser-only `detail` payload normalization fix, or should it also define fail-silent/no-reply behavior for unconfigured OpenAI/Codex provider failures at the routing boundary?
rationale: The parser gap is concrete, but silently discarding errors from providers a user has not configured changes provider diagnostics and channel-visible failure behavior, which needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Parser plus scoped routing policy
options.body: Add shared top-level `detail` support and explicit tests for unconfigured OpenAI/Codex failures that choose when the user sees a generic message, no reply, and where diagnostics are logged.

options.title: Parser-only narrow repair
options.body: Fix only the raw JSON `detail` leak now and leave provider probe gating or silent suppression to a separate canonical provider-routing issue.

options.title: Keep current diagnostics behavior
options.body: Reject silent suppression and only document that provider errors may surface as generic user-facing failures when a runtime path is invoked.

recommendation.title: Parser plus scoped routing policy
recommendation.body: Add shared top-level `detail` support and explicit tests for unconfigured OpenAI/Codex failures that choose when the user sees a generic message, no reply, and where diagnostics are logged.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent provider-routing and raw provider-error delivery history makes this the best available owner for the policy choice.
